question: Can genuine16 proposals using fewer quadrature points be cheap enough to save fine64 work?
fine_target: Existing shared64 R512/L1024 M256 Gauss128x128 BE dt.005 50steps, original temporal predictor/IC/damping/tolerances
quadrature: Classical tensor Gauss regenerated for each setting. No fitted EQ, no claimed physical mesh refinement; inherited analytic-advection/discrete-diffusion fine target unchanged.
proposals: One or two LM updates with genuine zero-tail D16, initialized by first16 coordinates of original fine predictor. History uses same fine accepted states and exact prefix test modes. Upward transfer is zero-padding. No learned P or field-fit restriction.
acceptance: Allow finite unfinished reason0 coarse proposal. Guard on original fine objective strict relative improvement1e-8; otherwise use original predictor. Fine damping remains original. Truncation loss recorded outside production timings.
quadrature_eligibility: On fixed six exposed cases at indices0,1,10,25,49 compare total r/J and nonlinear N/NJ versus G128 with SAME M. Each maxrelative<=1e-3, denominatorfloor1e-12. Development eligibility only.
validation: Exact original baseline counts and close states; field-preserving upward identity; disabled/forcedfail parity; fresh returned fine stationarity; timed/recorded witnesses
timing: 7 randomized paired full fused queries percase, burn before each; countall candidate/guard costs. Isolated component calls are separate diagnostics, not additive production attribution.
cost_gate: Median of per-case pairedmedianratios<=.85 and worstcase<=1.10; no exclusions or tuning. If none pass stop. Any cost win requires tightfine baseline agreement before speedupclaim.
scope: No training, sealed cohorts, 3D, repeated correction cycles, mesh changes or baseline changes
